story:
This carob has grown into a vault. Its lower limbs reach down until their ends rest on the ground, and the crown, about 17 by 15 metres and only 11 metres high, closes over the trunks so completely that from a distance you cannot see them. The Junta de Andalucia's register estimates its age at about 350 to 400 years, without saying how it arrived at that, and lists it for its age, its size and its peculiar shape.

Underneath are two trunks from one stool. The bigger one is almost hollow and measures 3.95 metres round at chest height, the other 2.65, and together they spread to 9.90 metres at the base. The register records it as a male tree.

The Canada Real Soriana, one of Spain's main drove roads for livestock, runs right beside it at the Loma de los Escalones, in farmland on the Sierra Morena side of Cordoba. Around it grow scattered rockrose and mastic, holm oaks, wild olives and stone pines.

It lies roughly nine kilometres north of the city centre, on public land that the drove road reaches. Nobody has described the way in on foot, no photograph of the tree has been published, and the pin is the register's point, so this is one for walkers willing to look. If you follow the Canada Real Soriana and find it, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the dome-shaped crown whose lower limbs rest on the ground, hiding two trunks. It stands beside the Canada Real Soriana drove road at the Loma de los Escalones, north of Cordoba.
